description: AI-assisted editorial summaries of upstream engineering work and owned public projects in Rudy Celekli’s portfolio.

addyosmani/agent-skills.title: Make the documented architecture gate detect a dependency cycle
addyosmani/agent-skills.problem: The constraint-driven development skill passed the source directory as a dependency-cruiser option argument. The tool printed usage and returned success even when its architecture rules should have blocked the change.
addyosmani/agent-skills.change: Run the checker against the source path with its ordinary config discovery. The documentation now gives a command that scans the tree.
addyosmani/agent-skills.validation: The pull request demonstrates a successful exit on the original command with a planted cycle, a failure with the corrected command, and a successful corrected run once the cycle is removed.

ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui.title: Preserving pending tool-call IDs in AG-UI's Go SDK
ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui.problem: The Go representation of a successful RUN_FINISHED outcome omitted the pending tool-call IDs. A Go relay could silently drop the information a frontend needed to resume with outstanding results.
ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui.change: The Go model now reads and writes those IDs on the success outcome and keeps them off other variants to match the protocol shape.
ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui.validation: The upstream fixture round-trips as JSON with the correction. The PR reports a revert-based failure control and 127 passing top-level Go tests.

agno-agi/agno.title: Keeping the last good Agno session table after a failed write
agno-agi/agno.problem: JsonDb started overwriting the live session table before serialization and writes completed. A file-size limit could leave a partial JSON document where a previously readable session table had been.
agno-agi/agno.change: The normal file path stages the serialized table in a unique sibling file and publishes it with an atomic replace after a successful close. Error cleanup removes the writer's own staging file, and the implementation preserves existing behavior for nonregular paths and file metadata described in the PR.
agno-agi/agno.validation: A subprocess reproduced a native EFBIG through the public session API. The PR records a 347-byte valid table becoming a 411-byte partial file on the baseline. With the patch, the original bytes remain readable and get_session returns the saved session.

AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.title: Returning an actionable exit status from claude-seo PageSpeed checks
AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.problem: The PageSpeed-only command stored errors below the selected strategies. Its process-exit check inspected a top-level field, so a pipeline could record success when every strategy failed.
AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.change: The result now exposes an overall error on total failure and preserves strategy details so the caller can inspect which request failed.
AgriciDaniel/claude-seo.validation: The merge record documents an offline trigger using an unsupported URL scheme. This tests command behavior without making a PageSpeed Insights request.

ai-job-search-dev/ai-job-search.title: Keep hidden markup out of job-research text extraction
ai-job-search-dev/ai-job-search.problem: The job research retry could expose text from an HTML template or an unclosed script block to its agent context. A truncated fetch was enough to surface text a browser would not display.
ai-job-search-dev/ai-job-search.change: Reuse the posting guard's hidden-block handling in the text-extraction path. Treat an unclosed hidden block as extending to the end of the input and keep visible text after properly closed blocks.
ai-job-search-dev/ai-job-search.validation: The pull request records a failing-then-passing extraction regression and 837 local tests passing with 30 skips. It separately reports four hosted CLI typecheck failures on unchanged code.

aindeev/agent-chrome-relay.title: Reclaiming Chrome tabs returned after agent disconnect
aindeev/agent-chrome-relay.problem: A Chrome tab could finish opening after the relay had swept the tabs of a disconnected agent. The late response then registered a tab with no connected owner. The same race affected popups.
aindeev/agent-chrome-relay.change: The relay marks the agent closed and checks that state before accepting late tab creation. It requests cleanup of the returned tab and drops queued page calls.
aindeev/agent-chrome-relay.validation: The PR reports two regressions at the deferred extension RPC boundary and a connected-agent control. The test uses the relay implementation with isolated RPC fixtures.

akitaonrails/ai-memory.title: Show unavailable storage measurements in ai-memory
akitaonrails/ai-memory.problem: A failed advisory SQLite read became a zeroed storage structure on the health page. Operators could see a false empty-database measurement and lose the accompanying reclaimability signal.
akitaonrails/ai-memory.change: Represent a failed read as unavailable. Keep the health page usable while rendering storage measurements and reclaim guidance according to whether the database statistics are known.
akitaonrails/ai-memory.validation: The pull request reports 29 passing health tests and 12 passing localization tests. Restoring the original behavior made two new health regressions fail.

Anil-matcha/suparagent.title: Separating Suparagent memories from fenced examples
Anil-matcha/suparagent.problem: A dated item inside a Markdown example could be read as a saved memory. Its sample date could also cause memory cleanup to remove it.
Anil-matcha/suparagent.change: The memory parser recognizes fenced code as example content before processing dated memory bullets. This keeps the example available to readers and out of memory accounting.
Anil-matcha/suparagent.validation: The merge record identifies a focused memory-budget regression and reports failure on the prior parser and success with the fix.

anmolkapil/plexo.title: Keeping spaces in filenames downloaded by Plexo
anmolkapil/plexo.problem: Some servers send Content-Disposition filenames with spaces and without quotes. Plexo stopped at the first space, turning quarterly report.csv into quarterly.
anmolkapil/plexo.change: The parser consumes the unquoted value through the next parameter separator and trims the surrounding spaces and tabs. Quoted and extended filenames continue to use their existing paths.
anmolkapil/plexo.validation: An Electron Playwright regression reproduced the truncated name. The merged record reports 32 passing download and redirect checks with the correction.

antchfx/htmlquery.title: Returning the XPath string value of an HTML document
antchfx/htmlquery.problem: HTML XPath queries could return an empty string when selecting the root document, even if descendant elements contained text. This affected string(/), root-context string(), and predicates that ask whether the document contains text.
antchfx/htmlquery.change: The navigator reuses the existing InnerText traversal for the document node, bringing its value into line with XPath's root-node string-value rule.
antchfx/htmlquery.validation: The regression tests cover root-context string and contains expressions and retain element and comment controls. The cited PR gives the XPath specification reference and reports local Go validation.

antchfx/jsonquery.title: Preserving JSON values through text and XML serialization
antchfx/jsonquery.problem: The Go JSON query library printed a native nil as Go's <nil> placeholder, although the original JSON value was null. XML serialization also wrote carriage returns literally, letting the XML parser normalize them to line feeds on a round trip.
antchfx/jsonquery.change: The text representation uses JSON's null spelling while retaining the native nil value. XML output writes carriage returns as character references so consumers can parse the original string back.
antchfx/jsonquery.validation: The two PRs report baseline-failing regression tests and successful full Go and race runs. The fixtures distinguish null from the string null, false and zero, and exercise carriage returns alongside CRLF, tabs and XML metacharacters.

antchfx/xmlquery.title: Keeping XML namespace declarations off the XPath attribute axis
antchfx/xmlquery.problem: xmlquery exposed xmlns and xmlns:p declarations through @*, altering attribute counts and positional predicates on namespaced XML.
antchfx/xmlquery.change: The XPath navigator skips namespace declarations when traversing attributes and keeps the source attribute representation available for XML serialization.
antchfx/xmlquery.validation: The contribution records passing Go and race checks with controls for ordinary attributes, xml:lang and serialized namespace declarations.

antchfx/xpath.title: Counting the actual following-axis nodes in XPath
antchfx/xpath.problem: The last() predicate counted siblings of a candidate node even when the expression selected through the following or following-sibling axis. That count could prevent the final matching node from being returned.
antchfx/xpath.change: The following query supplies the positional filter with the size of its own selected node set, cached for the current context node.
antchfx/xpath.validation: The PR reports an axis-specific mutation that reproduces the incorrect result, passing Go tests and agreement with lxml on a separate XML fixture.

areal-project/AReaL.title: Passing local worker environment values without losing delimiters
areal-project/AReaL.problem: The local scheduler serialized an environment dictionary into comma-separated key-value pairs. Commas in CUDA allocator settings and equals signs within values could then cause splitting errors before the worker launched.
areal-project/AReaL.change: The local scheduler passes the original mapping into the launcher utilities. The string interface remains available and splits a pair only on its first equals sign.
areal-project/AReaL.validation: The PR reports nine passing launcher tests, including two cases that fail without the correction. This validation runs in CPU-only tests and does not exercise launching a GPU worker.

AstrBotDevs/AstrBot.title: Keeping Telegram sender names useful in AstrBot context
AstrBotDevs/AstrBot.problem: Telegram permits accounts without a public handle. AstrBot represented every such sender as Unknown in history, model context and the nickname available to plugins, despite having a display name.
AstrBotDevs/AstrBot.change: The adapter selects the Telegram username first, then the display name, then Unknown. This preserves the existing username convention for accounts that already provide one.
AstrBotDevs/AstrBot.validation: The pull request reports a parametrized adapter regression across the username, display-name and empty-data cases, with 56 passing Telegram adapter tests. Telegram production usage is outside that test evidence.

Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon.title: Preserve exact JSON-RPC IDs through agent-beacon
Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon.problem: Decoding a request ID through float64 rounded some large integers. Two distinct client requests could receive the same response ID, interfering with response routing.
Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon.change: Retain numbers as json.Number and echo their exact JSON value in success and error responses. String IDs and dispatch behavior continue to use the existing path.
Asymptote-Labs/agent-beacon.validation: The pull request reports 24 transport cases through stdio and loopback HTTP, with eight baseline failures. The fixed package passed its ordinary and race checks locally.

backnotprop/plannotator.title: Opening a review note without accidentally posting the decision
backnotprop/plannotator.problem: Plannotator used Mod+Shift+Enter to open a note in plan review, but code review shared the primary submit handler without inspecting Shift. A reviewer following that shortcut could post an irreversible decision before entering the note.
backnotprop/plannotator.change: The review editor registers the note action and routes the shifted chord to the composer. The unshifted shortcut remains associated with the primary decision.
backnotprop/plannotator.validation: The PR records a DOM regression that detects a submitted decision on the baseline and expects an open composer with no submission on the repaired path. The case covers the editor's keyboard behavior.

bee-san/Ciphey.title: Keeping JavaScript character codes distinct from byte sequences in Ciphey
bee-san/Ciphey.problem: Ciphey stripped String.fromCharCode from decimal input and treated its arguments as UTF-8 bytes. The same integers can represent different text under JavaScript's UTF-16 rules.
bee-san/Ciphey.change: The decoder retains the explicit JavaScript interpretation and applies its code-unit conversion in the supported numeric grammar. Bare decimal input follows the byte-decoding path.
bee-san/Ciphey.validation: The PR used Node as an independent oracle for ambiguous values and surrogate controls. It reports 2,420 local Rust tests passing and separately discloses an owned qualification run marked failed for its spelling command.

bee-san/pyWhat.title: Scanning literal directory names in pyWhat
bee-san/pyWhat.problem: Recursive identification interpreted user-supplied path components as part of a glob. A directory named scan[2026] could be skipped, while an asterisk could select an unintended sibling.
bee-san/pyWhat.change: The identifier escapes the directory path before appending the recursive glob, keeping glob syntax limited to the search portion it adds.
bee-san/pyWhat.validation: End-to-end fixtures verify discovery in the selected directory and absence of decoys from a sibling. The recorded cases went from three failures to three passes.

bee-san/RustScan.title: Preserving TOML and script metadata semantics in RustScan
bee-san/RustScan.problem: Documented lowercase script modes were rejected by the config reader. The script metadata reader also removed every hash from a line, changing values such as language tags and URL fragments.
bee-san/RustScan.change: The parser accepts documented lowercase aliases alongside the existing variant names and continues to reject unknown strings. Script metadata extraction removes only the leading comment marker, leaving embedded punctuation for TOML to interpret.
bee-san/RustScan.validation: The config PR exercises the public Config::read path through temporary files and reports a baseline where the three lowercase cases fail. The metadata PR uses the real parser with a temporary fixture and checks the complete command-format string without executing it or scanning a network.

beenuar/AiSOC.title: Reading all available Entra audit pages in AiSOC
beenuar/AiSOC.problem: The Entra connector consumed only the first response page from Microsoft Graph. More than 200 matching audit or risky-sign-in entries in a poll could leave older entries unread before the next polling window.
beenuar/AiSOC.change: The connector follows the supplied @odata.nextLink for both feeds. It retains completed pages when a later request fails and warns at the 25-page limit.
beenuar/AiSOC.validation: A focused fixture retrieved 680 entries across both feeds and reproduced first-page loss when the source change was reverted. The merge record also notes existing test-environment failures and the absence of a live tenant run.

benbjohnson/litestream.title: Keeping Litestream's WAL read lock through request cancellation
benbjohnson/litestream.problem: A control-socket sync could open a long-lived SQLite read transaction using the short-lived request context. On return, database/sql rolled the transaction back while Litestream still held a pointer and treated the lock as active. Automatic checkpointing could then restart the WAL before replication read the newest frames.
benbjohnson/litestream.change: The change gives the read transaction a lifetime independent of the caller's cancellation, so it remains active until Litestream's lock management finishes with it.
benbjohnson/litestream.validation: The linked issue reproduction ran twice per binary. The PR records WAL restart and failing replica integrity checks for TXIDs 3 through 6 in both baseline runs, with neither failure in the two candidate runs. This evidence covers the reproduced control-socket setup.

bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.title: Wrap Local ADS-B track labels at north
bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.problem: The ADS-B decoder supplies tracks in a half-open range from zero up to 360 degrees. Rounding 359.7 degrees in the card yielded 360, inconsistent with north labels elsewhere in the globe interface.
bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.change: Wrap the whole-degree display after rounding so a track rounding to due north reads zero. The change is confined to the card model's display value.
bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.validation: The pull request reports a fixture changing from 360 to zero and five passing card localization tests. No live aircraft feed was required.

cathrynlavery/diagram-design.title: Preserving type syntax in draw.io imports
cathrynlavery/diagram-design.problem: A plain draw.io label such as List<U> could lose its type parameter when the importer treated angle brackets as HTML. Applying entity decoding twice could also change the intended label.
cathrynlavery/diagram-design.change: The importer now checks each cell's html=1 style before applying HTML cleanup. That decision covers node labels, edge labels and labels on edge children.
cathrynlavery/diagram-design.validation: The merged contribution reports an import verifier with plain-text and HTML controls, plus the project's local validation commands. The report discloses Codex assistance.

chunkhound/chunkhound.title: Distinguishing the official VoyageAI endpoint from look-alike hosts
chunkhound/chunkhound.problem: ChunkHound classified an endpoint as official using a raw prefix check. Hostnames that appended a subdomain or hyphen suffix to api.voyageai.com could therefore enter configuration branches intended for VoyageAI's official service.
chunkhound/chunkhound.change: The check now requires the exact official base or a slash boundary after it, matching the guard used for the analogous OpenAI endpoint helper.
chunkhound/chunkhound.validation: The author reports eight focused cases covering official forms and suffix spoofing. Reverting the implementation made both spoofing assertions fail again. The helper was loaded directly for local testing because the full package's optional parser and database dependencies were unavailable.

CopilotKit/OpenBot.title: Preserving shared OAuth registrations across OpenBot replicas
CopilotKit/OpenBot.problem: A replica unable to decrypt an OAuth client could interpret the read fault as absence and register a replacement. Changing the shared pointer made the existing client unavailable to a healthy replica.
CopilotKit/OpenBot.change: Both reads, including the one inside the registration lock, distinguish typed credential-read faults and stop before registration. The connection route records a durable audit event and returns a retryable 503.
CopilotKit/OpenBot.validation: The PR describes controls with real encrypted rows and different keys, plus database route tests. The candidate preserved the existing pointer and made zero vendor registrations in the fault cases.

coreyhaines31/marketingskills.title: Validate OneSignal audiences before sending a request
coreyhaines31/marketingskills.problem: The marketing CLI forwarded arrays or scalars where OneSignal's notification endpoint required an alias map. Its segment route also accepted invalid filter entries and out-of-range counts.
coreyhaines31/marketingskills.change: Check that aliases form a dictionary and that the segment contains one to 200 filter or operator objects. Preserve shorthand aliases and leave field-level interpretation to the provider.
coreyhaines31/marketingskills.validation: The pull request reports 22 affected contract tests and 899 passing CLI and asset tests in isolation. Delivery requests were mocked.

cursor/plugins.title: Selecting the current pull request in Cursor's stack orchestrator
cursor/plugins.problem: A branch can have a historical closed or merged pull request and an active replacement. Treating those rows as equivalent makes the stack orchestrator reject a branch that has one unambiguous current review.
cursor/plugins.change: The stack store selects the sole active PR when present. It retains historical anchors when no active PR exists and still rejects a genuinely ambiguous branch with multiple active PRs.
cursor/plugins.validation: The co-authored upstream diff adds tests for an active replacement alongside both closed and merged history, plus a control with two active PRs. Additional credited commits bound polling sleeps by the deadline and distinguish fork heads during discovery.

debpalash/OpenGTM.title: Encode untrusted lead data for spreadsheet exports
debpalash/OpenGTM.problem: OpenGTM's API and CLI wrote scraped lead strings into CSV. Spreadsheet programs can treat values beginning with formula markers as executable formulas when a user opens the export.
debpalash/OpenGTM.change: Apply the same string-escaping policy across both lead export paths. Preserve numeric values and restricted phone-like strings while neutralizing formula prefixes.
debpalash/OpenGTM.validation: The pull request reports regressions for the API route, CLI path and string cases, plus 44 passing related tests. That evidence covers export encoding behavior.

debpalash/VoiceStudio.title: Protecting busy VoiceStudio sidecar processes
debpalash/VoiceStudio.problem: An engine-level unload could kill a sidecar while it was handling a request. A duplicate unload override bypassed the reaper's existing operation-lock check.
debpalash/VoiceStudio.change: The engine now reaches the guarded unload path, where busy sidecars remain available and idle ones can shut down and respawn on demand.
debpalash/VoiceStudio.validation: The PR reports a reproduction using the shipped echo sidecar with its operation lock held and 51 focused checks of the corrected behavior. The offline fixture used native subprocesses and did not perform GPU synthesis.

deeplethe/utopia.title: Interpret numeric weekdays consistently in Utopia schedules
deeplethe/utopia.problem: The Advanced scheduling field advertised standard cron while the evaluation library mapped numeric weekdays differently. An expression entered as Monday through Friday could fire Sunday through Thursday.
deeplethe/utopia.change: Normalize numeric weekday expressions to named weekdays using standard cron semantics before storing new values. Previously stored numeric expressions keep their original behavior until resaved.
deeplethe/utopia.validation: The pull request reports a baseline Sunday firing and a corrected Monday firing in an isolated Rust fixture pinned to the scheduler library. It does not report a full workspace build.

dosco/graphjin.title: Discover inherited OpenAPI response fields in GraphJin
dosco/graphjin.problem: GraphJin's OpenAPI introspection saw direct declarations but could miss fields inherited through allOf. Composed objects and array-item schemas could lose discoverable columns or result paths.
dosco/graphjin.change: Combine the relevant schema constraints across composition branches and reuse the resolved view for queries and mutations. Leave the loaded component schemas intact.
dosco/graphjin.validation: The PR reports a before-and-after regression for composed array items and passing OpenAPI package checks with the race detector. HTTP fixtures cover result extraction and component immutability.

e2e-inc/e2e.title: Collect several browser downloads from one test action
e2e-inc/e2e.problem: An export can produce multiple files from a single click. The existing single-download path also let a stalled file transfer outlive its timeout.
e2e-inc/e2e.change: Add a collector that runs one trigger and gathers the requested number of downloads in start order. Use one timeout for start, completion and saving, and clean up started transfers when the wait aborts.
e2e-inc/e2e.validation: The pull request reports local Chromium and provider-path fixtures covering multiple files and stalled transfers, with 609 passing web-package tests.

earthtojake/text-to-cad.title: Preserving native CAD worker failure reasons in the Viewer
earthtojake/text-to-cad.problem: When a CAD daemon worker crashed or was killed, the Viewer could report a failed update without the diagnostic the process had already provided. This left both native crashes and intentional cancellation hard to distinguish at the job boundary.
earthtojake/text-to-cad.change: The daemon now records a worker's exit code or terminating signal as the job's failure reason. The maintainer rebased the contributor patch and integrated it alongside existing telemetry.
earthtojake/text-to-cad.validation: The maintainer's upstream commit explicitly credits the original PR and contains a daemon-client regression. A separate credited commit preserves daemon-channel descriptor ownership during cancellation. These changes concern recorded job state and transport ownership.

fabio-rovai/open-ontologies.title: Reject truncated XML before loading ontology records
fabio-rovai/open-ontologies.problem: A cut-off XML document could contain one complete record and one unfinished record. The importer loaded the completed prefix and reported success, concealing lost data.
fabio-rovai/open-ontologies.change: Reject end-of-file while element depth remains open, before mapping or loading records. Preserve valid handling of complete documents, including self-closing elements, CDATA and empty fields.
fabio-rovai/open-ontologies.validation: The PR records nine passing Linux integration checks after eight baseline failures. The validation includes the built command-line tool and file-dispatch paths.

facebookresearch/swe-sweep.title: Accounting for grader crashes in SWE-Sweep
facebookresearch/swe-sweep.problem: A grader crash writes a short reward record with a failure marker. The score reader expected fields from a completed trial, so a crashed trial could vanish from evaluation failure counts.
facebookresearch/swe-sweep.change: The scorer checks the explicit grader_failed marker before requiring completed-trial fields. It reports the crash and keeps the trial out of the headline score.
facebookresearch/swe-sweep.validation: The merged test plan covers scoring and grader-failure records, including the distinction between a crash and a file that is merely incomplete.

facelessuser/wcmatch.title: Interpreting an empty glob root as the current directory
facelessuser/wcmatch.problem: A caller passing an empty string or empty bytes for root_dir could get different results than a caller using the expected current directory. The behavior also mattered when the calling process supplied a directory file descriptor.
facelessuser/wcmatch.change: The attributed upstream commit treats either empty root representation as the current directory, including within the directory descriptor's scope. It uses native path separators in test expectations to reflect Windows and POSIX behavior.
facelessuser/wcmatch.validation: The upstream commit contains the regression and changelog entry. Its coauthor trailers credit Isaac Muse and Claude Sonnet 5.5 alongside the attributed contribution.

go-resty/resty.title: Normalizing Resty load-balancer URLs before joining request paths
go-resty/resty.problem: A base URL with a fragment or a bare question-mark could absorb the request path when combined with the caller's relative URL. In the fragment example, a caller requesting /requested reached the upstream server's root.
go-resty/resty.change: The client clears fragment-related fields and the empty-query marker alongside its existing base-path and query normalization.
go-resty/resty.validation: The regression uses a loopback HTTP server through Resty's public load-balancer API. The PR reports three baseline failures and a passing ordinary-query control, followed by four passing cases and a passing full Go suite on the candidate.

google-deepmind/concordia.title: Preserving choice labels in Concordia's simulation components
google-deepmind/concordia.problem: A choice offered through a hidden component wrapper needs a stable label so the simulation can identify the inner choice. The wrapper previously obscured the label that the caller expected to use.
google-deepmind/concordia.change: The upstream Copybara import exposes the inner choice label. A separate attributed import accepts sequences of component keys in narrative situation handling.
google-deepmind/concordia.validation: The public commits identify Rudy Mizrahi Celekli as the original author and preserve imported revision provenance. This case records the simulation-library API work. The commits provide no empirical social-simulation result.

google-research/harness2.title: Rejecting conflicting judge verdicts in Google Research Harness²
google-research/harness2.problem: The bundled LAB grader could take the first fenced JSON verdict before checking for disagreements. A response containing a pass example and a later fail verdict could therefore write a pass score.
google-research/harness2.change: The patch routes every fenced verdict through the existing agreement check. Ambiguous responses retry, and exhausting retries leaves no cached score.
google-research/harness2.validation: The PR reports ten offline tests through pinned LAB code, the score writer and Harness²'s adapter using scripted judge responses. The checks exercise evaluator behavior without calling a model.

google-research/timesfm.title: Aligning TimesFM covariate residuals with the available backcast
google-research/timesfm.problem: TimesFM 2.5 sized covariate residuals from the full input even when the model cropped context. For very short inputs, a zero-length slice could unexpectedly select the full series.
google-research/timesfm.change: The residual window follows the context the model sees. The fit handles an empty residual series without invalid statistics and reports a clear error if every series is too short.
google-research/timesfm.validation: The PR reports six focused tests using a randomly initialized Torch model, checking output shapes and finiteness for long, short and mixed batches. That experiment measures shape handling.

Graphicle-AI/graphicle.title: Returning the correct JSON-RPC error for unavailable Graphicle methods
Graphicle-AI/graphicle.problem: A workspace MCP connection returned Invalid params when it received a method that the connection did not expose. That made capability absence indistinguishable from an invalid request to a supported method.
Graphicle-AI/graphicle.change: The dispatch layer now returns -32601 for an unavailable method. Errors such as an unknown tool within tools/call still use -32602.
Graphicle-AI/graphicle.validation: The merge record reports 690 local Rust tests and identifies a workspace-scope control for both error codes.

Graphify-Labs/graphify.title: Resolving Python graph edges to the method named in source
Graphify-Labs/graphify.problem: Graphify assigned separate identifiers to methods such as run and _run, but the member-call resolver folded the names together when choosing a target. A valid call could therefore point to the wrong node in the graph.
Graphify-Labs/graphify.change: The attributed fix resolves a member call using the method spelling. Related commits harden evidence checks for mis-cased confidence values and keep parallel relations when exporting Obsidian notes.
Graphify-Labs/graphify.validation: The upstream commit records preserve the implementation and attribution. The cases concern graph fidelity at extraction and export boundaries, and provide no measured claim about retrieval performance.

harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science.title: Reject non-finite numbers in a scientific benchmark evaluator
harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science.problem: A scientific output verifier parsed floating-point values and accepted non-finite representations as numeric findings. That let malformed values satisfy the shape of a finding without providing a usable estimate.
harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science.change: Check finiteness after numeric parsing and retain the benchmark's existing missing-value path. Leave the scientific scoring method and admissible finite values unchanged.
harbor-framework/terminal-bench-science.validation: The pull request reports negative controls for non-finite and overflow values, plus passing finite and missing-value controls. The evidence is local verifier testing.

HarnessRouter/harnessrouter.title: Normalize tool-call deltas across valid SSE encodings
HarnessRouter/harnessrouter.problem: HarnessRouter's DSH relay expected a space after the SSE data-field colon. Valid streams with no space bypassed cleanup, so empty continuation fields could erase an accumulated tool name and ID.
HarnessRouter/harnessrouter.change: Match the data field independent of its optional space, then apply the existing normalization to JSON objects. Leave non-object events and unrelated fields alone.
HarnessRouter/harnessrouter.validation: The pull request reports 18 focused cases passing, with the new case failing when the old guard is restored. The broader local suite recorded 31 failures.

harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo.title: Generate from prepared video assets without an LLM credential
harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo.problem: MoneyPrinterTurbo's setup helper required LLM credentials for callers who already supplied narration and either local footage or stock-search terms. Those inputs already bypass the corresponding text-generation steps.
harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo.change: Inspect the effective script and terms options before deciding whether to ask for an LLM credential. Keep the material-provider checks that the selected asset path still needs.
harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo.validation: The pull request reports three baseline failures, a missing-terms control and 54 passing helper tests. A CLI import test was deselected because optional media dependencies were absent. No live video generation was exercised.

haydenschmitty/floorplan.title: Mapping routes through real framework boundaries in Floorplan
haydenschmitty/floorplan.problem: A codebase map can make incorrect inferences if it mistakes syntax for evidence. Floorplan lost Hono routes after reading a wildcard inside a string as a comment. Django child routes lost their mount prefix, while Express checks could leak from one route into the next.
haydenschmitty/floorplan.change: The changes preserve source positions while recognizing quoted strings, interpret Django include calls as mounts, and scope each Express middleware scan to that route call. Where the route uses a separately named handler, the extractor excludes the handler from the middleware list.
haydenschmitty/floorplan.validation: The PRs include fixtures with a Hono wildcard, a Django orders mount, and Express routes using named handlers. The recorded outputs show the affected routes appearing and the Express fixture identifying its actual unchecked routes. This evidence concerns static extraction from those fixtures.

headroomlabs-ai/headroom.title: Removing provider outages from Headroom answer scores
headroomlabs-ai/headroom.problem: Evaluation paths converted provider exceptions to ordinary answer strings. Two identical error messages could score as a perfect match, and a diagnostic that named the expected answer could receive credit.
headroomlabs-ai/headroom.change: Failed calls now populate the existing error state and bypass answer scoring and judge evaluation. A successful response containing the literal text ERROR remains eligible for normal scoring.
headroomlabs-ai/headroom.validation: The documented baseline awarded 2 of 2 cases in each affected evaluator. After the change, a controlled failure and one valid response correctly produced 1 of 2. The figures are fixture results.

HelixDB/helix-foundry.title: Keep a completed Helix Foundry answer when Stop arrives late
HelixDB/helix-foundry.problem: A cancellation request could arrive just after an analyst run completed and overwrite its successful status. The saved answer remained, but follow-ups disappeared and retry could re-run the question.
HelixDB/helix-foundry.change: Refuse cancellation of a succeeded run with a conflict response and leave its answer and status in place. Preserve cancellation behavior for active runs and repeated requests for stopped runs.
HelixDB/helix-foundry.validation: The PR reports 11 passing thread tests and passing related route checks. The regression exercises an already-completed run at the API boundary.

heygen-com/hyperframes.title: Encoding Hyperframes feedback that ends at an emoji boundary
heygen-com/hyperframes.problem: The feedback command could truncate between two UTF-16 surrogate units. URL encoding the partial emoji then threw an exception before the issue URL was available.
heygen-com/hyperframes.change: The truncator removes a trailing high surrogate if its matching low surrogate was cut off, while keeping the established limits and ellipsis.
heygen-com/hyperframes.validation: A focused Vitest run found two baseline failures and recorded nine passes with the correction. Complete emoji at the boundary and ordinary ASCII were included as controls.

HKUDS/DeepTutor.title: Speak LaTeX degree superscripts correctly in DeepTutor
HKUDS/DeepTutor.problem: DeepTutor expanded the circle command as function composition before examining superscripts. A decimal or symbolic angle reached the speech layer as garbled prose.
HKUDS/DeepTutor.change: Recognize the circle command in superscript position before expanding ordinary operators. The same command still means composition when it appears between functions.
HKUDS/DeepTutor.validation: The pull request reports 45 passing focused speech-processing tests and 68 passing voice service tests. Those checks cover the pre-TTS behavior.

HKUDS/nanobot.title: Preserving spreadsheet cell provenance and inline media in Nanobot
HKUDS/nanobot.problem: Nanobot reconstructed spreadsheet coordinates by counting tab characters in text. A tab inside a cell was indistinguishable from a delimiter, so search results could cite the wrong Excel column. Its media reader also rejected a valid data URL when the base64 marker used uppercase letters.
HKUDS/nanobot.change: The workbook extractor records actual cell starts and uses those offsets to report search matches. The media parser accepts the marker case-insensitively while retaining strict payload checks. The media PR records a maintainer follow-up that uses delimiter parsing to avoid pathological header matching.
HKUDS/nanobot.validation: Workbook regressions exercise actual XLSX files through the grep tool, with coverage for tabs within a cell and empty leading cells. The media PR records a two-case before/after test and 21 passing decoder tests at the contributor's tested revision. The cases document local input handling.

HKUDS/Vibe-Trading.title: Require enough observations for strict factor statistics
HKUDS/Vibe-Trading.problem: A single information-coefficient observation in Vibe-Trading could produce a success row with NaN sample deviation. Strict JSON consumers could not serialize that result.
HKUDS/Vibe-Trading.change: Use the same minimum sample size as the ordinary factor runner. The strict path records one-observation alphas as skipped and keeps its existing empty-series reason.
HKUDS/Vibe-Trading.validation: The pull request reports a baseline failure and 44 passing strict-runner tests after the change. The new test serializes the result with strict JSON settings. The checks are offline.

ifixai-ai/iFixAi.title: Verify iFixAi policy repair reports before export
ifixai-ai/iFixAi.problem: A Policy Lab export accepted a submitted repair report without confirming its relationship to the underlying search. A substituted bundle or altered minimality claim could therefore appear as valid evidence.
ifixai-ai/iFixAi.change: Rerun the bounded local search at export, compare canonical digests across the full report, and export the recomputed result when they match. Reject discrepancies before creating output.
ifixai-ai/iFixAi.validation: The pull request reports four baseline failures and 82 passing Policy Lab tests after the change, including the CLI export route. The checks use synthetic offline evidence.

jaredwray/cacheable.title: Rejecting malformed duration literals before cache TTL conversion
jaredwray/cacheable.problem: The shorthand TTL parser could interpret a malformed duration as valid by parsing a numeric prefix. For callers this makes a bad setting look accepted while producing an expiry time different from what they entered.
jaredwray/cacheable.change: The change matches the full decimal-and-unit expression and confines decimal parsing to a single optional group. The converter can then apply the supported time unit to a validated number.
jaredwray/cacheable.validation: The PR records regressions for malformed numeric inputs and controls for valid shorthand. These checks address parsing and conversion, with cache behavior downstream dependent on how callers handle invalid values.

JetBrains/thinkrail.title: Preserving unsent image drafts when ThinkRail chats remount
JetBrains/thinkrail.problem: Switching tabs unmounted the chat composer. Its text draft survived because it belonged to the session, but pasted and attached images disappeared with the UI component.
JetBrains/thinkrail.change: The change moves attachment drafts and their pending decode state into the corresponding chat runtime. Accepting a submission clears the draft, and resetting or replacing the runtime prevents an old decode from restoring an attachment to a closed session. A second PR fixes Markdown list markers in settled answers.
JetBrains/thinkrail.validation: The image PR records before/after browser screenshots and covers remounts, isolation across chats, submission reset and pending decodes. The list PR documents browser checks for wrapping, nested lists and exact-source clipboard output.

JustVugg/colibri.title: Isolate simultaneous model download jobs in Colibri
JustVugg/colibri.problem: A millisecond timestamp served as a model download's job ID. When two jobs started in the same millisecond, the second registry entry displaced the first and cancellation could target the wrong worker.
JustVugg/colibri.change: Give each download a separate UUID while retaining the timestamp for display and sorting. The existing cancellation route accepts the resulting hex identifiers.
JustVugg/colibri.validation: The pull request records two failing-then-passing regressions covering the real local HTTP path and 64 concurrent job registrations on a fixed clock. It reports 28 passing UI gateway tests and one skip, using synthetic download metadata.

kenn-io/agentsview.title: Reading compressed OpenClaw transcripts without blocking host sync
kenn-io/agentsview.problem: OpenClaw's transcript schema allows plain event JSON or a compressed zstd blob. Scanning a NULL JSON column into a Go string stopped host synchronization as soon as AgentsView encountered a compressed event.
kenn-io/agentsview.change: The parser checks for the compressed column, decodes bounded zstd frames, and fingerprints valid events consistently across plain and compressed storage. Malformed data remains isolated to its own session so healthy siblings can continue.
kenn-io/agentsview.validation: The PR records a real SQLite test database containing alternating plain and compressed events, with equal fingerprints and parsed messages for equivalent data. It reports passing parser and sync tests. The fixture uses standard zstd framing and does not establish compatibility with a captured production archive.

Kentucky-ai/opentakeoff.title: Opening the rest of an OpenTakeoff archive after a bad image
Kentucky-ai/opentakeoff.problem: A damaged PNG or JPEG in a ZIP could abort the whole import loop, keeping later valid plans off the canvas.
Kentucky-ai/opentakeoff.change: Each extracted file now runs through the existing per-file error handling, which identifies the unreadable image and continues with the rest.
Kentucky-ai/opentakeoff.validation: The merge record compares two malformed archives with real fflate extraction. The corrected importer returned both later PDFs and one skipped image in each case.

ktwu01/benchmark-radar.title: Preserving partial arXiv results in Benchmark Radar
ktwu01/benchmark-radar.problem: In the opt-in Atom reader, a later query failure could trigger an RSS fallback that discarded successful earlier Atom results. RSS can omit older papers updated during the overlap period.
ktwu01/benchmark-radar.change: The fallback now combines successful Atom records with exact-ID RSS additions and exposes a degraded-source warning. If no source succeeds, the operation still reports failure.
ktwu01/benchmark-radar.validation: Offline cases cover an Atom paper missing from RSS, duplicates, and empty or failed RSS. The PR reports 186 passing source tests and identifies Atom multi-query as opt-in.

ktwu01/benchmark-radar-paper.title: Synchronizing Benchmark Radar's research attribution across manuscript outputs
ktwu01/benchmark-radar-paper.problem: The Benchmark Radar manuscript needed to reflect the accepted coauthor invitation consistently in the source byline, affiliation mapping and compiled PDF metadata.
ktwu01/benchmark-radar-paper.change: The merged edit adds Rudy Mizrahi Celekli with his Gradia affiliation and describes his work on corpus identity preservation and report reliability. It updates the author-mapping regression, rebuilds the manuscript and retains the frozen benchmark evidence.
ktwu01/benchmark-radar-paper.validation: The PR reports 25 passing Python checks, successful verification of the frozen v0.11.0 artifacts, and visual and metadata inspection of a Tectonic build. Local LaTeXML was unavailable. The merge verifies the manuscript update.

lightpanda-io/browser.title: Making Lightpanda respect browser message and selector contracts
lightpanda-io/browser.problem: Lightpanda delivered window messages without checking the recipient origin the caller supplied. Its DevTools selector lookup also returned an error for a valid selector with no match, which caused clients that poll for late elements to stop early.
lightpanda-io/browser.change: The browser validates and carries the intended origin through the asynchronous window-message task, then checks the receiving document's current origin before dispatching. The DevTools handler uses a successful response with node ID zero for an empty match and preserves separate error paths.
lightpanda-io/browser.validation: The window tests include cross-origin and malformed-origin cases, same-origin defaults and wildcard behavior. The PR reports that reverting only the implementation makes the regression fail. The selector PR gives a minimal Chrome-versus-Lightpanda DevTools exchange that explains the polling contract.

lightseekorg/tokenspeed.title: Treating token ID zero as a valid end-of-sequence ID
lightseekorg/tokenspeed.problem: TokenSpeed used a truthiness check when collecting model and generation EOS IDs. Zero is a valid token ID, but it could be treated as absent or cause a type error when combined with a set of generation IDs.
lightseekorg/tokenspeed.change: The merged config change includes EOS ID zero in the same normalization and union path as other explicit IDs.
lightseekorg/tokenspeed.validation: The PR describes a real ModelConfig loaded from a small temporary Qwen3 configuration. Three of seven fixture cases failed on the baseline, and all seven passed on the candidate. This test covers configuration behavior.

liliang-cn/cortexdb.title: Check vector dimensions before CortexDB index training
liliang-cn/cortexdb.problem: CortexDB already enforced dimensionality when adding or searching vectors. Its IVF training path could still panic on a short vector or produce centroids of the wrong width from a longer one.
liliang-cn/cortexdb.change: Validate every training vector's dimension before running k-means or mutating index state. The error identifies the out-of-shape input.
liliang-cn/cortexdb.validation: The pull request records a baseline panic and passing Go package tests with short, long and nil-vector coverage. It does not report a full repository race run.

liseami/CCBaga.title: Passing literal known_hosts paths to OpenSSH from CCBaga
liseami/CCBaga.problem: OpenSSH reads UserKnownHostsFile values with its own quoting rules. A valid filename containing a double quote could make that parser fail before a connection attempt began.
liseami/CCBaga.change: CCBaga escapes quotes and backslashes inside the quoted path, keeping the whole setting in a single -o argument.
liseami/CCBaga.validation: The focused tests call local ssh -G and compare the parsed path for embedded spaces, a quote and a backslash. The run exercised configuration parsing without a VPS connection.

lz4/lz4.title: Reading complete short skippable LZ4 frames
lz4/lz4.problem: The file reader applied the normal-frame minimum header size before distinguishing skippable frames. A complete eight-byte frame with an empty payload could therefore be rejected as if it were a truncated normal frame.
lz4/lz4.change: The reader parses the frame type before applying the normal-frame minimum, allowing short but complete skippable frames. A separate Meson patch sets the C language for two static-library options that previously failed during configuration.
lz4/lz4.validation: The frame PR reports 189 passing tests in each of the serial and multithreaded unit builds, including a matrix across all 16 skippable magic values and short payloads. The Meson evidence covers setup for both options and compilation for the endianness option. The allocation-disabled build still exposed a separate compilation issue.

mark3labs/mcp-go.title: Resetting event type at MCP Go stream boundaries
mark3labs/mcp-go.problem: A Server-Sent Events block with a type field and no data could leave the type set for the next block. The legacy transport could then discard an ordinary JSON-RPC response under the wrong event name.
mark3labs/mcp-go.change: Both stream readers clear the event type at every blank-line boundary, including blocks without data, so a later data-only block receives the default message type.
mark3labs/mcp-go.validation: The merged record shows a failing regression in each reader before the correction and reports both passing afterward.

max-sixty/worktrunk.title: Letting Worktrunk recover after a failed worktree lookup
max-sixty/worktrunk.problem: Calling the plugin command before git init cached a null result for that directory. The same plugin process kept returning the miss after a worktree became available. A transient process failure could produce the same stale state.
max-sixty/worktrunk.change: The lookup now caches successful locations while retrying failures on subsequent commands. Positive caching still avoids unnecessary Git probes, and passive hooks continue to record directories without triggering lookups.
max-sixty/worktrunk.validation: The PR reports a canonical Claude Code plugin test that starts without a repository, makes one available and verifies the subsequent pane opens. All nine canonical plugin tests passed on the reported candidate. The PR documents the tradeoff of repeat probes when every lookup fails.

maziyarpanahi/openmed.title: Generate internally consistent synthetic FHIR collections
maziyarpanahi/openmed.problem: Synthetic clinical demos need realistic links between encounters, observations and the underlying patient. An isolated collection can look plausible even when its references, provenance or event ordering fail validation.
maziyarpanahi/openmed.change: Build offline FHIR R4 fixture collections from explicitly synthetic journey facts. Check typed reference closure, shared subjects, source provenance and temporal ordering through independent controls.
maziyarpanahi/openmed.validation: The pull request records 29,569 passing tests and 186 skips on the candidate. Coverage applies to the documented fixture subset. Full FHIR or implementation-guide certification was outside its scope.

milind-soni/OpenMausBot.title: Protecting spreadsheet export semantics and encoded secrets
milind-soni/OpenMausBot.problem: A conservative CSV formula guard also escaped valid signed numbers, turning negative amounts into spreadsheet text. The secret scrubber missed some form-encoded spellings of held passwords because browser form serialization escapes several characters that encodeURIComponent leaves intact.
milind-soni/OpenMausBot.change: The CSV serializer preserves plain signed numeric cells while escaping formula-like expressions. The login vault adds the spelling produced by URLSearchParams to its scrubber candidates, covering cases such as a held secret containing an exclamation mark represented as %21.
milind-soni/OpenMausBot.validation: The linked regressions target the table CSV path and the login scrubber. The CSV test retains a formula control, and the masking PR includes an encoding example that distinguishes browser form serialization from URI component encoding.

mohit67890/imajev.title: Serving text-only Qwen requests without torchvision
mohit67890/imajev.problem: ImAjev eagerly constructed a multimodal processor during startup. For text-only CPU serving, this activated a video-processor import and prevented the server from starting when torchvision was absent.
mohit67890/imajev.change: The change loads the tokenizer first, lazily constructs the full processor for image inputs, and preserves tokenizer padding through that transition. A text-only install extra makes the supported configuration explicit.
mohit67890/imajev.validation: The PR reports 28 passing focused tests and three skips, with CPU text-logit and image parity checks on a small generated Qwen checkpoint. The offline full suite retained four baseline failures. Released weights and native Windows ARM64 were outside that validation.

morluto/jacobian.title: Installing Jacobian in the active Claude Code profile
morluto/jacobian.problem: Jacobian setup wrote configuration and skills under the home directory even when CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pointed Claude Code at a separate profile. Setup could report completion while the active profile saw neither installation.
morluto/jacobian.change: The setup and detection code use the selected directory for .claude.json and skills, falling back to the home-directory layout when no override is configured.
morluto/jacobian.validation: The PR describes isolated setup tests for custom and default profiles. The result covers local configuration paths.

morluto/leantoken.title: Keeping LeanToken benchmark evidence bounded and interpretable
morluto/leantoken.problem: A blocking read from an MCP child could outlast the readiness budget. Nonfinite values in the paired benchmark threshold could also allow a significant slowdown through the regression gate. Either condition undermines repeatable comparisons.
morluto/leantoken.change: The benchmark client now shares one absolute readiness deadline across retries and notifications, invalidates unusable streams, bounds frame size and wakes blocked callers on close. The paired evaluator rejects thresholds outside the finite float range. The npm launcher also forwards subsequent signals while its child remains alive.
morluto/leantoken.validation: The PRs describe executable peers that reproduce incomplete frames and notification floods, a CLI threshold regression with finite-value controls, and a child fixture that receives two signals through the launcher. The npm fixture used a Node child, and the checks establish behavior in these harnesses.

morluto/rea.title: Honor the declared ELF header boundary in rea
morluto/rea.problem: rea checked table offsets against the minimum header size for the ELF class. An ELF file with an extended declared header could point a program or section table back into those header bytes and still be admitted.
morluto/rea.change: Compare each populated table's offset with the validated declared header size. Preserve acceptance when a table starts at or beyond the header boundary.
morluto/rea.validation: The pull request reports four regressions failing on the original code and all 19 tests in the declared-range suite passing afterward. Fixtures cover ELF32, ELF64 and both byte orders.

msitarzewski/agency-agents.title: Explain the 14.4× incident-alert burn rate correctly
msitarzewski/agency-agents.problem: An availability SLO example described its 14.4× alert as predicting budget exhaustion in two hours. An on-call engineer reading that comment would get the wrong estimate for the configured 30-day window.
msitarzewski/agency-agents.change: Correct the explanation to about 50 hours at a sustained 14.4× rate. The one-hour observation window corresponds to roughly 2% of a 30-day error budget. The alert expression itself is unchanged.
msitarzewski/agency-agents.validation: The pull request shows the calculation against the example and its 6× companion rule. It reports a clean scoped lint check.

mvschwarz/openrig.title: Show OpenRig mission labels after proof acceptance
mvschwarz/openrig.problem: An OpenRig mission declared complete could still display a qualified label asking for proof review when its current evidence was already ready. That label confused two decisions an operator needs to see independently.
mvschwarz/openrig.change: The dashboard formatter uses the authored completion label when both the declaration and proof support it. Active or paused declarations and incomplete or mixed proof keep their qualified labels.
mvschwarz/openrig.validation: The pull request records five failing formatter cases on the baseline and 1,784 passing UI tests after the fix. Its full test command still exited with four daemon-suite failures.

NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra.title: Preserving Android sparse-image bytes in Ghidra
NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra.problem: FILL chunks reversed their four-byte pattern. DONT_CARE chunks left zero bytes out of the checksum, and a skipped region exactly the size of the 1 MiB buffer could produce no output.
NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra.change: The decoder preserves the stored fill order and emits skipped regions in bounded blocks, applying each block to the checksum.
NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra.validation: The linked case documents the 1 MiB boundary and the validation revision. The contribution discloses Codex implementation and identifies the earlier verification run as historical because it predates source-only cleanup.

NousResearch/hermes-agent.title: Revalidating worktree state before Hermes cleanup
NousResearch/hermes-agent.problem: Worktree state can change between checking it and actually removing it. Cleanup needs to keep its decision tied to the current worktree state at the point the potentially destructive action runs.
NousResearch/hermes-agent.change: The attributed Hermes commit revalidates cleanup gates before removing a worktree. Other upstream commits by the same contributor reject nonstandard JSON before file writes and reject negative retention before pruning backups.
NousResearch/hermes-agent.validation: The default-branch commit records establish the source changes and include their cherry-pick provenance. This case documents the guard and leaves production usage unmeasured.

Nutlope/hallmark.title: Matching whole job aliases in Hallmark
Nutlope/hallmark.problem: Hallmark's draw command replaced recognized aliases inside longer values. It could transform application into trylication and then tell the caller that no job was supplied.
Nutlope/hallmark.change: Alias lookup now uses the whole input. The command can report an unknown supplied value separately from an omitted argument.
Nutlope/hallmark.validation: The PR documents seeded CLI examples for supported aliases such as app and newsletter, as well as unknown and omitted arguments.

open-compass/VLMEvalKit.title: Count failed video-model API responses as incorrect
open-compass/VLMEvalKit.problem: VLMEvalKit marked failed API predictions with a score of minus one. Video benchmark aggregation used truthiness, so that sentinel boosted accuracy instead of registering a failed prediction.
open-compass/VLMEvalKit.change: Count a prediction as correct only when its score is exactly one, while keeping failed rows in the denominator. Align overall and per-dimension aggregation with the correctness predicate.
open-compass/VLMEvalKit.validation: The PR records two before-and-after aggregation tests. In the fixture, one correct result out of four was previously displayed as 75% and now computes to 25%.

openclaw/goplaces.title: Keeping proxy queries and request paths distinct in goplaces
openclaw/goplaces.problem: Appending a Places endpoint suffix to the raw base URL could put the operation into a proxy query parameter. An override such as /v1/?tenant=one acquired a modified tenant value instead of dispatching to the intended Places operation.
openclaw/goplaces.change: The upstream consolidation integrates the URL fix from PR #74. It joins parsed path components while retaining escaped path segments and existing proxy queries, and distinguishes a Routes base prefix from an already complete computeRoutes endpoint.
openclaw/goplaces.validation: The original reproduction records loopback HTTP requests from the actual CLI and public Go consumers, plus Go build and race checks. The upstream diff includes an endpoint-query regression and credits the original reports. The loopback fixture uses a dummy credential.

openclaw/mcporter.title: Passing explicit empty values through the MCPorter CLI
openclaw/mcporter.problem: The CLI discarded empty positional strings after the literal separator. A caller sending an explicit empty text value to an MCP tool therefore sent an absent argument, which the server schema rejected.
openclaw/mcporter.change: The upstream consolidation incorporates the fix from PR #412, preserving argument positions after the literal separator, including empty strings and flag-like values intended as tool input.
openclaw/mcporter.validation: The original PR records a real CLI subprocess and local SDK echo server. The baseline rejects the missing string, while the patched request returns an empty text item. The credited upstream consolidation reports 2,128 passing tests and exact-head cross-platform CI.

openclaw/openclaw.title: Keeping Feishu code examples intact in OpenClaw agent context
openclaw/openclaw.problem: An incoming Feishu code block containing triple backticks could prematurely close the Markdown wrapper. An agent then received code and unintended prose as separate pieces.
openclaw/openclaw.change: The Feishu renderer selects a fence longer than any backtick run in the message's code, with a minimum of three.
openclaw/openclaw.validation: The merge record documents a built Gateway with a local HTTPS Feishu fixture and signed webhook inputs. An independent parser recovered one intact code node in the corrected capture. The capture intercepted the message before model execution.

openclaw/Peekaboo.title: Carry rounded durations into the next unit in Peekaboo
openclaw/Peekaboo.problem: Peekaboo could display 59.95 seconds as 60.0 seconds even though 60 seconds used a minutes label. The same inconsistency appeared at the microsecond and millisecond boundaries in its activity views.
openclaw/Peekaboo.change: Share rollover behavior across the compact and detailed formatters. After rounding, carry values into the appropriate next unit and handle unrepresentable inputs.
openclaw/Peekaboo.validation: The pull request reports passing cases for 13 compact, seven detailed and four unrepresentable duration values in the Swift formatter suite.

OpenMontageInc/OpenMontage.title: Keeping usable OpenMontage assets in a size-limited cache
OpenMontageInc/OpenMontage.problem: A generated image larger than the entire cache could push out every smaller asset and still leave the cache over its configured limit.
OpenMontageInc/OpenMontage.change: The cache checks the size of a new entry before least-recently-used eviction. Diagram generation can still return the valid image because cache admission is optional.
OpenMontageInc/OpenMontage.validation: The PR reports a local Pillow diagram reproduction with a 512-byte cache, a roughly 2.4 kB output and a previously cached 76-byte image. The corrected path preserves both the generated output and the cached image. The checks ran offline.

opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox.title: Clean up stale Jupyter contexts after a sandbox restart
opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox.problem: OpenSandbox kept a cached code context when Jupyter's delete endpoint returned 404. If Jupyter restarted or otherwise lost its session, repeated deletes failed and bulk cleanup stopped at the stale context.
opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox.change: Classify the missing session as already absent and remove local context entries. Other Jupyter failures keep the existing error path.
opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox.validation: The pull request reports a regression using an HTTP test Jupyter server that returns 404 and passing existing creation and deletion suites afterward.

orestbida/cookieconsent.title: Discarding cookie-consent drafts consistently
orestbida/cookieconsent.problem: Closing preferences without saving restored the visual switches but left an internal draft of enabled services. A user could reopen the panel and save without touching the switches, unknowingly committing the discarded selection.
orestbida/cookieconsent.change: The discard path rebuilds the draft from the restored checkbox values. The subsequent save reflects the state the reopened panel displays.
orestbida/cookieconsent.validation: The documented jsdom regression turns on a service, closes without saving, reopens and saves without changes. It fails before the patch and passes after. The PR reports 120 passing tests and a successful build, with real-browser testing outside the reported checks.

Panniantong/Agent-Reach.title: Rejecting invalid Agent-Reach configuration before saving
Panniantong/Agent-Reach.problem: Falsy YAML values such as false, 0 or an empty list could be accepted as an empty mapping and then overwritten. Non-string keys could also crash later key processing.
Panniantong/Agent-Reach.change: The loader rejects unsupported document shapes and non-string mapping keys up front. Empty and null documents remain valid configuration inputs.
Panniantong/Agent-Reach.validation: The PR reports a focused suite moving from seven failures to all eleven passing, alongside 618 full-suite passes. It separately records existing SDK type-check failures.

paperclipai/paperclip.title: Keeping unread agent comments visible in Paperclip inboxes
paperclipai/paperclip.problem: New comments moved an assigned issue forward in recency sorting. By reusing that issue update time as a fallback read receipt, Paperclip could treat the arriving comment as already read and hide it from an assignee's unread inbox.
paperclipai/paperclip.change: The maintainer ported the original fix onto the current branch with explicit contributor credit. It uses creation time for the assignee's initial read boundary, preserves explicit read receipts and excludes deleted external comments from unread calculations.
paperclipai/paperclip.validation: The upstream commit describes native PostgreSQL regressions for real comment writes, later assignment and deleted comments. It reports 41 focused tests passing on the frozen head and successful hosted build, typecheck and end-to-end shards. The original PR remains separately linked as provenance.

proffesor-for-testing/agentic-qe.title: Keep generated tests out of Agentic QE execution results
proffesor-for-testing/agentic-qe.problem: The MCP test generator returned code and also stored each generated object as a test outcome. In that path, defaults could create a passing result and an execution duration before any test ran.
proffesor-for-testing/agentic-qe.change: Remove the execution-result insertion from the generation path. Preserve generated code in the response and keep measurement paths for observed execution and coverage.
proffesor-for-testing/agentic-qe.validation: The pull request reports that six generation regressions failed on the original handler factory and all 32 cases passed after the change. The fixture mocks the factory's dependencies.

raphaelmansuy/edgequake.title: Propagate request encoding failures from the EdgeQuake Swift SDK
raphaelmansuy/edgequake.problem: The Swift SDK discarded encoding errors while building HTTP bodies. It could send a POST, PUT or PATCH with the body missing and leave the caller debugging a misleading server error.
raphaelmansuy/edgequake.change: Propagate the original encoding error before dispatch and update the multipart caller to handle the throwing request builder.
raphaelmansuy/edgequake.validation: The pull request reports failing-then-passing method regressions that verify no request is sent after an encoding error. It reports 237 passing Swift tests and 22 skipped live end-to-end tests.

retentioneering/retentioneering-tools.title: Making Retentioneering calendar-day metrics independent of the host
retentioneering/retentioneering-tools.problem: DuckDB resolved timezone-aware timestamps to calendar dates in the session timezone. Identical events around UTC midnight could count as one or two active days on different machines.
retentioneering/retentioneering-tools.change: The SQL expression now converts timezone-aware inputs through UTC before taking the date. The same rule serves metrics, daily states and conditional event collapse, and naive timestamps use their direct date cast.
retentioneering/retentioneering-tools.validation: The PR records a two-event fixture under four host timezones. Three previously reported one active day and all four reported two after the correction.

rociiu/talorys.title: Keeping recent edits when importing a Talorys backup
rociiu/talorys.problem: Importing an older backup could silently replace newer local task, project and note text because their upserts overwrote existing rows without checking recency.
rociiu/talorys.change: The backup importer updates those three record types only if the incoming timestamp is strictly newer, extending the rule that already protected memory records.
rociiu/talorys.validation: A focused regression in the merge record restores stale versions of all three record types and checks that local edits survive. A newer note then confirms that legitimate updates can still import.

rudycelekli/agntcs-marketing-assets.title: A versioned public image handoff
rudycelekli/agntcs-marketing-assets.problem: A marketing image can be difficult to identify when its only reference is an attachment or a mutable working link.
rudycelekli/agntcs-marketing-assets.change: The AGNTCS asset repository assigns committed paths to public Instagram imagery so a reviewer can refer to a specific revision when inspecting a creative handoff.
rudycelekli/agntcs-marketing-assets.validation: The repository describes an asset collection. The source does not establish campaign reach or asset performance.

rudycelekli/ai-movie-maker.title: Turning story formulas into a production plan
rudycelekli/ai-movie-maker.problem: A scene-generation pipeline needs to preserve story structure and character decisions across generation steps.
rudycelekli/ai-movie-maker.change: The project represents formulas as JSON and separates formula interpretation, character management, AI routing, and production-plan modules. It includes a local test-flow entry point and reference notes.
rudycelekli/ai-movie-maker.validation: The public source supports the pipeline decomposition. Provider execution, rendered-film quality, and usage require separate evidence.

rudycelekli/bolt-generated-project.title: A small browser game with explicit component boundaries
rudycelekli/bolt-generated-project.problem: A game prototype needs to keep input, gameplay coordination, and enemy state understandable as behavior grows.
rudycelekli/bolt-generated-project.change: The Space Invaders prototype uses an HTML entry point and separates the Game, Player and Enemy modules in JavaScript. The revision exposes those component boundaries for inspection.
rudycelekli/bolt-generated-project.validation: The pinned source supports the architectural description. The study records no browser compatibility, latency, or playability measurement.

rudycelekli/code-transplant.title: Moving a TypeScript parser with a behavioral reference
rudycelekli/code-transplant.problem: A parser can compile after extraction and still change outputs when its dependency environment shifts.
rudycelekli/code-transplant.change: Code Transplant extracts a named parser with a dependency capsule and explicit adapter. It compares the adapter against the unchanged source parser on concrete inputs and preserves a verification record.
rudycelekli/code-transplant.validation: The source documents a replayable comparison. Agreement is scoped to the observed inputs and the selected parser.

rudycelekli/effinai.title: Packaging agent workflows as a plugin marketplace
rudycelekli/effinai.problem: A developer needs a discoverable installation route when agent, tool, and skill definitions are distributed together.
rudycelekli/effinai.change: Effin.AI documents a Claude Code marketplace installation and organizes capabilities for users who install the plugin. The public repository makes its published catalog inspectable.
rudycelekli/effinai.validation: The documentation supports the packaging and installation design. The listed integrations and runtime capabilities require execution with their dependencies.

rudycelekli/es-atlas.title: Separating an agent persona from deployment wiring
rudycelekli/es-atlas.problem: A consulting assistant needs editable role instructions alongside a repeatable way to package its runtime.
rudycelekli/es-atlas.change: Atlas keeps the role in a skill document and the runtime in deployment and entrypoint files. A nested consulting skill contains Python code and a memory module.
rudycelekli/es-atlas.validation: The pinned tree supports the packaging design. Instructional examples in the repository are not deployment evidence.

rudycelekli/ghostpart.title: A planar repair part from a calibrated phone photo
rudycelekli/ghostpart.problem: A phone image gives pixel positions, while replacement mounting plates need physical dimensions.
rudycelekli/ghostpart.change: GhostPart uses a calibration reference to estimate mounting-point locations from a photo and outputs an editable, printable replacement plate. The design includes a fit revision loop and geometry suited to planar work.
rudycelekli/ghostpart.validation: The experimental release documents printed and paperless reference modes and a guided accuracy check. Actual tolerance depends on the capture setup and part geometry.

rudycelekli/gradia-blocks.title: Reviewable admission for reusable capabilities
rudycelekli/gradia-blocks.problem: Reusable components can carry implicit tenant, event, and retry assumptions into workflows that depend on them.
rudycelekli/gradia-blocks.change: Gradia Blocks packages runnable references for Feedback, Work Items, Event Relay and Outbox. A separate admission screen evaluates candidates, and source-pinned Skills describe how to use the references.
rudycelekli/gradia-blocks.validation: The repository documents these component contracts and admission mechanics. Deployment and isolation properties depend on the consuming implementation.

rudycelekli/gradia-guard.title: Binding a verifier to a declared execution boundary
rudycelekli/gradia-guard.problem: An execution record is only interpretable if a reviewer knows which part of the system was observed.
rudycelekli/gradia-guard.change: Gradia Guard pairs a local recorder with a verifier for explicit execution boundaries. The SDK and optional AG-UI edge record evidence for specific integration surfaces.
rudycelekli/gradia-guard.validation: The public beta documentation describes the local verifier and the limits of voluntary SDK instrumentation. Stronger enforcement requires separate runtime evidence.

rudycelekli/gradia-lens.title: Reversible interventions on a pinned model
rudycelekli/gradia-lens.problem: Model intervention results are hard to interpret when model versions or restoration behavior change between runs.
rudycelekli/gradia-lens.change: Gradia Lens gives researchers a local CPU path to intervene on pinned GPT-2 components, measure effects, and restore the original state for replay.
rudycelekli/gradia-lens.validation: The public alpha covers the documented GPT-2 path. Cross-model generalization needs separate experiments.

rudycelekli/gradia-range.title: Replayable adversarial tasks in synthetic twins
rudycelekli/gradia-range.problem: Testing a risky agent workflow against a live system can expose operational data and make outcomes hard to reproduce.
rudycelekli/gradia-range.change: Gradia Range describes cloning a system into a synthetic twin, slicing it into witnessed tasks, and producing replayable verdicts. Humans and agents attempt tasks on separate boards.
rudycelekli/gradia-range.validation: The source documents the evaluation design and release timing. Synthetic coverage depends on how faithfully the chosen twin represents the workflow.

rudycelekli/gradia-reward-loop.title: Tracing reward hacking into an RL diagnostic
rudycelekli/gradia-reward-loop.problem: A scorer exploit can matter differently once it becomes a training signal.
rudycelekli/gradia-reward-loop.change: Gradia Reward Loop carries oracle-witnessed pass/wrong pairs into a training-time experiment and records evidence bundles for replay. The project describes a paired GRPO diagnostic with single-variable localization.
rudycelekli/gradia-reward-loop.validation: The pinned source supports the documented diagnostic design. A broader effect on policy training needs independent replication and holdouts.

rudycelekli/gradia-universes-work-sample.title: Exactly-once replay after a simulated interruption
rudycelekli/gradia-universes-work-sample.problem: An agent can resume its work using information that became stale while it was stopped.
rudycelekli/gradia-universes-work-sample.change: Gradia Universes models a synthetic world change and records the resulting visibility, interruption, restore, and authoritative-state checks. The fixture lets a reviewer inspect whether a change was applied exactly once.
rudycelekli/gradia-universes-work-sample.validation: The repository supplies a bounded synthetic work sample. The replay claim is scoped to that universe.

rudycelekli/gradia-wind-tunnel.title: Testing a benchmark scorer against an oracle
rudycelekli/gradia-wind-tunnel.problem: An evaluator can accept a wrong answer when the reward logic checks a proxy for correctness.
rudycelekli/gradia-wind-tunnel.change: The Wind Tunnel compares a scorer decision with an independent machine oracle and localizes exploitable differences using single-variable changes. Replayable records connect an exploit to the exact comparison.
rudycelekli/gradia-wind-tunnel.validation: The public evidence concerns the tested scorer, oracle, and examples. Other evaluators require separate calibration and adversarial evidence.

rudycelekli/kin-connect.title: Dual approval in agent-mediated introductions
rudycelekli/kin-connect.problem: A successful policy match between two agent profiles can still produce an introduction that either person would decline.
